explain.say: When you throw a stone, you give it two motions at once: forwards and upwards. After it leaves your hand, gravity is the main force acting on it.

explain.say: Forwards, nothing much slows it, so it keeps moving sideways at nearly the same speed. Upwards, gravity slows it every second until, at the top, it stops rising.

explain.say: Then gravity speeds it back down. Steady forward motion plus falling makes a smooth curve called a parabola, the same shape as the jets of a fountain.

explain.say: Without air, throwing at 45 degrees sends a stone furthest. In real air, drag shortens the flight, so the best angle is usually a little lower.

faq.q: Why does a thrown ball come back down?
faq.a: Gravity pulls it down the whole time it is in the air. It slows the ball as it rises, stops it rising at the top, and then speeds it up as it falls.
asks: What makes a thrown ball fall?

faq.q: What shape does a thrown stone make?
faq.a: Its path is a curve called a parabola. Without air it is symmetrical: the stone rises and falls in the same shape.

faq.q: What angle throws a stone furthest?
faq.a: Without air resistance, 45 degrees gives the longest throw on level ground. With air, and when you throw from shoulder height, a slightly lower angle usually goes further.
asks: What is the best angle to throw?

faq.q: Does a stone keep moving forward while it falls?
faq.a: Yes. Gravity only pulls down, so it doesn't slow the stone's sideways motion. Only air resistance slows it forwards.
asks: Why does gravity not stop the forward motion?

faq.q: Does a dropped stone land before a thrown one?
faq.a: If both start at the same height at the same moment, a stone dropped and a stone thrown straight sideways land together. Gravity pulls them down at the same rate; the thrown one just travels further sideways.
asks: Does throwing something sideways make it fall slower?

facts: Without air resistance, a thrown object follows a parabola, a path explained by Galileo.
Ignoring air resistance, a launch angle of 45 degrees gives the greatest range on level ground.

quiz.say: You throw a stone forwards and upwards. At the highest point of its flight, what is it doing?
quiz.show: At the top of its flight, a thrown stone is…

options.show: Still moving forwards, but not rising
options.say: Still moving forwards, but not rising

quiz.why: Gravity has stopped its upward motion, but nothing has stopped its forward motion, so it is moving sideways at the top.

wrong.1: Only its upward motion has stopped; it is still moving forwards.
wrong.2: Gravity slows the upward motion; it never speeds it up.
